headline: 18 km completed: recover now, not more mileage
summary: Post-run update: 18.07 km in 1h 50m 50s at 6:08/km, average HR 157 and maximum 174 using a chest strap confirmed by Nelson. Garmin load was 228 and aerobic effect 4.6. This was a substantial session after only 5h 09m sleep, not the short easy run recommended this morning.

recommendation.title: No more training today; prioritize recovery
details: No additional running or cycling today. Eat a normal carbohydrate-rich meal with protein, drink to thirst and cool down comfortably.
Tomorrow: recovery day with optional 20–30 minutes relaxed walking at RPE 1–2; reassess after a full night’s sleep.
Do not add a long run, quality work or make-up distance this weekend.
recommendation.alternative: Complete rest if tired, sore or unwell; walking is optional.
recommendation.reduce_or_stop: Stop for pain that changes gait, illness, unusual fatigue or dizziness. Seek urgent care for chest pain, fainting or severe breathlessness.

signals.label: Substantial physiological cost
signals.interpretation: Garmin classifies the run as lactate threshold. This is not proof of actual threshold intensity throughout, but it was not a low-cost recovery run.

signals.label: Historical fitness comparison
signals.interpretation: Today’s 6:08/km at 157 bpm is broadly encouraging against October 2024 but less efficient than the selected October 2025 runs. Temperature, duration, route and unknown historical sensor sources prevent a quantified fitness change.

caveats: Device measurements and classifications are Garmin data; the recommendation is coaching judgment.
Garmin’s recovery timer estimates readiness for another hard effort; it is not a ban on all movement.
Current alertness, symptoms and medical advice override device scores.
Chest-strap use today is user-confirmed; historical sensor sources are unverified. Historical comparisons use selected September–November 2024/2025 Sydney runs of 14–22 km, not controlled tests.
Weather source: https://www.bom.gov.au/products/IDN60901/IDN60901.94768.shtml — 24 October 2026, 12:30 AEDT; station conditions do not establish conditions along the entire route.
Fitness assessment: treat today as endurance training with high recovery cost. Repeated comparable cool-weather, rested, chest-strap runs are needed to separate fitness from heat and fatigue.

run_assessments.assessment: 18.07 km in 1h 50m 50s (6:08/km), average HR 157, maximum 174, ascent 101 m, load 228, aerobic effect 4.6 and anaerobic effect 0.0. Nelson confirms chest-strap HR for this run; take the elevated HR seriously rather than dismissing it as wrist-sensor error. The 30–40 minute conditional easy recommendation was exceeded substantially; perceived effort and symptoms are unknown. Garmin recorded 26–30°C. BOM Observatory Hill at 12:30 measured 22.5°C, humidity 71% and dew point 17.0°C: a city-station observation near the start, not a route-wide measurement. Humidity and warmth plausibly increased cardiovascular demand; no fixed heat correction or measured cardiac drift can be established from the available summary. Historical spring Sydney comparators: 17 Oct 2024, 21.23 km, 6:19/km, HR 160, ascent 83 m, device 22–28°C; 8 Oct 2025, 18.01 km, 5:43/km, HR 141, ascent 84 m, device 23–27°C; 15 Oct 2025, 20.01 km, 5:36/km, HR 139, ascent 97 m, device 22–29°C. Today was 11 sec/km faster and 3 bpm lower than the 2024 example, but 25–32 sec/km slower and 16–18 bpm higher than these 2025 examples. Different durations and unidentified older HR sensors limit inference. Endurance is intact, but this single heat-affected run does not establish improvement or a return to 2025 aerobic efficiency.
